level: In-depth engineering course · no official exam
name: System Design for Builders
audience: Senior engineers, architects and founders who design, build and run production systems with small teams.
format: This site's course with a 40-question practice test of estimation, trade-off, failure-mode and design-review questions.
scenarios: Building a payments or order pipeline
Designing an LLM gateway and RAG service
verifyNotes: This is the site's own in-depth engineering course, not a vendor certification: there are no exam facts to confirm, so spend Research on finding the best official/primary sources per topic (URLs that will be cited as sources) and on what is current as of November 2026. Goal: a senior engineer or architect who builds products alone or in a team of 2-3 can apply every idea confidently in real work, a design review or a senior interview. Lessons go deep: intuition first, then the precise mechanism, then a fully worked example with real numbers or code, then where it matters in production, then a common misconception. Write math in LaTeX between double dollars only: $$...$$; NEVER single-dollar math (single $ renders literally; in SQL or shell code use code fences). In JSON strings escape backslashes. Markdown tables: never put a raw | inside a cell (escape it as \\| or use \\lvert in math). Every lesson has a hands-on lab: a small exercise with the expected output. State any randomness seed. Question mix: ~45% trade-off and judgment in a concrete scenario, ~25% estimation or compute (QPS, storage, bandwidth, latency budgets, availability math, queueing), ~30% failure modes and debugging a design. Verifiers check every computed number with /Users/ashotpahlevanyan/MyProjects/maark/claude-cert/web/.pipeline/py313/bin/python (CPython 3.13). Prefer designs a team of 1-3 can operate (managed services, Postgres first, few moving parts) and say when a bigger-company pattern is overkill. Name products only as examples; keep claims vendor-neutral unless a source backs them. Sources: the AWS Builders' Library and Well-Architected Framework, Google SRE books (sre.google), Azure Architecture Center cloud design patterns, Google Cloud Architecture Center, Raft and other primary papers, IETF RFCs, official docs of PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, OAuth/OpenID, OWASP, and Martin Fowler's site; no Medium, no interview-prep blogs.

domains.name: Requirements, estimation and reliability targets
skills: Functional vs non-functional requirements; turning vague asks into numbers
Back-of-the-envelope estimation: QPS, peak factors, storage, bandwidth, latency numbers
Availability math: nines, serial and parallel dependencies, SLIs, SLOs and error budgets
Latency: percentiles, tail latency and fan-out, Little's law and queueing intuition
CAP, PACELC and consistency models (linearizable, sequential, causal, eventual, read-your-writes)

domains.name: Data storage, replication and caching
skills: Choosing storage: relational first, when key-value, document, wide-column, search or object storage fit
Replication: leader-follower, multi-leader, leaderless quorums; replication lag and its anomalies
Partitioning and sharding: key choice, hot keys, rebalancing, consistent hashing
Transactions and isolation in practice: anomalies, optimistic vs pessimistic concurrency
Caching: cache-aside, write-through, TTLs and invalidation, stampedes, CDN and HTTP caching

domains.name: Scalability and resilience patterns
skills: Load balancing (L4 vs L7), stateless services, horizontal scaling and autoscaling
Timeouts, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, retry budgets and retry storms
Circuit breakers, bulkheads, load shedding and graceful degradation
Rate limiting algorithms: token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed and sliding windows; distributed limits
Idempotency keys, deduplication and safe retries for writes and payments

domains.name: Asynchronous and distributed systems
skills: Queues vs logs: delivery semantics (at-most-once, at-least-once, effectively-once), ordering and partitions
The transactional outbox, change data capture and the dual-write problem
Sagas and compensation vs distributed transactions (2PC); event sourcing and CQRS at a working level
Consensus and leader election at a working level (Raft), leases and fencing tokens
Time in distributed systems: clock skew, logical clocks, why wall clocks lie

domains.name: APIs, multi-tenancy and security
skills: API styles: REST, gRPC, GraphQL, webhooks and server-sent events; when each fits
API design: pagination (cursor vs offset), versioning, errors, idempotent methods (RFC 9110)
Authentication and authorization: sessions vs tokens, OAuth 2.0 and OIDC flows, JWT pitfalls
Multi-tenancy: pooled vs siloed data, tenant isolation, row-level security, noisy neighbours
Security by design: least privilege, secrets, encryption in transit and at rest, OWASP Top 10

domains.name: Design case studies, observability and cost
skills: Classic designs: URL shortener, news feed (fan-out on write vs read), chat and presence, notification system
Search and autocomplete; file uploads and media processing pipelines
Designing AI systems: an LLM gateway, a RAG service, background agents and their cost and latency
Observability: metrics, logs, traces, RED and USE methods, alerting on SLO burn rate
Cost-aware architecture for small teams: managed services, build vs buy, avoiding premature distribution
